question: What is the primary function of the proximal colon during digestion?
explanation: The proximal colon extracts water and mineral electrolytes from the liquid chyme, converting it into solid or semisolid fecal matter as it moves distally. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: What physiological event immediately triggers the conscious urge to defecate?

options.C: Release of gastrin in the stomach
options.D: Contraction of the internal anal sphincter

explanation: When stool enters the rectum, the walls stretch, which stimulates sensory nerve endings and triggers the neural reflex creating the urge to evacuate. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which medication class is well-known for directly slowing colonic motility through enteric receptor binding?
explanation: Opioid analgesics bind to mu-opioid receptors in the gastrointestinal tract, inhibiting peristalsis and significantly increasing fluid absorption from stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: What characterizes pelvic floor dyssynergia as a cause of constipation?

options.A: Complete absence of colonic peristaltic waves
options.B: Paradoxical contraction of pelvic floor muscles during evacuation
options.C: Excessive secretion of mucus by the rectal mucosa
options.D: Rapid transit of stool through the transverse colon

explanation: In defecatory disorders, the muscles that should relax to allow passage instead tighten inappropriately, blocking the exit pathway. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which symptom is considered a red flag requiring urgent investigation in a patient with new-onset constipation?
explanation: Unexplained weight loss, alongside rectal bleeding or anemia, strongly suggests an organic pathology like a malignancy rather than simple functional constipation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: A digital rectal examination is performed on a patient complaining of severe constipation. What is a primary clinical purpose of this assessment?

options.A: To stimulate immediate high-amplitude peristaltic contractions
options.B: To collect a baseline sample for routine urinalysis
options.C: To evaluate sphincter tone and check for fecal impaction
options.D: To measure exact colonic transit time directly

explanation: Digital examination allows the clinician to feel the consistency of stool in the vault, check for masses, and assess resting and squeeze anal tone. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: How do osmotic laxatives primarily relieve constipation?

options.A: By absorbing excess gas and softening the outer fecal coating
options.B: By directly irritating the colonic mucosa to speed up peristalsis
options.C: By paralyzing the internal anal sphincter for easier passage
options.D: By drawing water into the intestinal lumen through osmotic pressure

explanation: Osmotic agents are poorly absorbed substances that retain fluid within the bowel lumen, keeping stools soft and bulky. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which classification of laxatives works best by directly stimulating myenteric nerve endings in the colon?
explanation: Stimulants like senna increase intestinal motility by acting directly on the mucosal nerve plexuses of the large intestine. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is it important to increase fluid intake when recommending a high-fiber diet to a patient?

options.A: To prevent the rapid breakdown of fiber into simple sugars
options.B: To activate the kidneys to produce hormones that stimulate peristalsis
options.C: To dilute digestive enzymes so they do not irritate the stomach lining
options.D: To prevent the fiber from forming a dense, obstructing mass in the bowel

explanation: Bulk-forming fiber requires sufficient water to swell properly; without adequate fluids, dry fiber can worsen constipation or cause impaction. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: A patient asks when is the best time to attempt having a bowel movement to take advantage of natural body rhythms. What is the best response?

options.A: Twenty to thirty minutes after finishing a meal
options.B: Right before going to bed at night
options.C: In the middle of the afternoon during peak activity
options.D: Immediately upon waking up before drinking anything

explanation: Eating triggers the gastrocolic reflex, which naturally increases colonic motility and creates an optimal window for successful evacuation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is a primary clinical consequence of a severe, prolonged fecal impaction?

options.A: Spontaneous healing of chronic anal fissures
options.B: Paradoxical overflow diarrhea around the mass
options.C: Rapid acceleration of upper gastrointestinal transit
options.D: Excessive production of pancreatic digestive enzymes

explanation: When hard stool blocks the rectum, liquid stool from higher up can slip around the impaction, presenting as sudden fecal incontinence or diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which preventive nursing action is most effective for a bedridden patient newly started on strong opioid therapy?

options.A: Initiating a prophylactic bowel regimen with stool softeners and stimulants
options.B: Encouraging heavy weightlifting exercises in bed
options.C: Waiting until the patient complains of pain before intervening
options.D: Restricting daily oral fluid intake to prevent bladder distension

explanation: Because opioids consistently slow bowel transit, proactive laxative therapy prevents constipation before it develops into impaction. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)
